search_text: Abstract : There is evidence for an enormous elliptical Impact Crater with the dimensions of 1270 x 950 km on the ocean floor of the Arctic Ocean. This elliptical impact crater and the dynamic effects of the ejected material have formed the deep sea basin area below -3000 m in the Beaufort Sea (Arctic Ocean) and triggered an expansion tectonics process. This assumed impact crater seems to be responsible for the Permian-Triassic boundary ~253 million years ago, which has caused the biggest mass extinction in Earth’s history. The Permian-Triassic(PT)-ImpactCrater was formed by an oblique impact.
